newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand PM Chavalit optimistic about economy.
newsitem.headline: Thailand PM Chavalit optimistic about economy.

text.p: Thailand's Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Wednesday expressed confidence that the economy would recover from its current malaise.
The country was going through a period of adjustment after a decade of rapid growth but fundamentals remained strong, he told a group of local and foreign business leaders.
"This is not the first time a country has experienced short-term financial difficulties, and I dare say it won't be the last," he said.

"However, I am confident that the fundamentals of the Thai economy remain strong... By focusing on stability over growth, I have no doubt that we will make the Thai economy more efficient, enabling us to enter the new century with a bright economic outlook," he added.

Chavalit said the tighter fiscal policy taken by the government and recent measures to bolster the troubled financial sector would help Thailand in the long run. The government is also taking measures to boost exports which contracted by 0.2 percent in 1996 after string 23 percent growth in 1995.
The government had recently trimmed spending by 100 billion baht ($3.85 billion) amid an economic slowdown to maintain a balanced budget and narrow a wide current account deficit.
"The...budget cuts and decisive financial sector reforms represent strong medicine. But in order to put our house in order, it is medicine we must swallow," he said.
